key_concept: Here 'polarity' means overall solvent polarity, set mainly by the polar functional group and its hydrogen-bonding ability ($-COOH$ > $-OH$ > $>C=O$ > $-O-$), not just the bare dipole-moment value.
steps: A, diethyl ether ($C_2H_5OC_2H_5$): the $C-O-C$ bond is only weakly polar. The two $C-O$ dipoles partly cancel across the bent geometry, and the ether has no $O-H$ hydrogen to donate in hydrogen bonding. It is the least polar ($\mu \approx 1.15\,D$).

C, acetone ($CH_3COCH_3$): the $>C=O$ group is strongly polar because of resonance ($C^{\delta+}=O^{\delta-}$). It can only accept hydrogen bonds and cannot donate them, so it is more polar than the ether but less polar than the H-bonding liquids.
B, ethanol ($C_2H_5OH$): the $O-H$ group both donates and accepts hydrogen bonds. This gives a strongly associated, highly polar liquid, more polar than acetone in solvent terms.

D, acetic acid ($CH_3COOH$): it carries both a $>C=O$ and an $O-H$ group. The $O-H$ is made even more polar by the adjacent carbonyl, and the acid forms strong H-bonded dimers. It is the most polar of the four.
Increasing order of polarity: $A < C < B < D$, which matches option (4).
why_not_others: Options (2) and (3) place acetone below the ether, ignoring the strongly polar $C=O$ group. Option (1) places ethanol below acetone, ignoring that the $O-H$ group's hydrogen bonding makes alcohols more polar solvents than ketones.
common_trap: Students rank purely by tabulated dipole moments, where acetone ($\approx 2.9\,D$) exceeds ethanol and acetic acid ($\approx 1.7\,D$), whereas the expected answer uses overall polarity governed by hydrogen bonding.
time_saving_tip: Rank by functional group using the chromatography/solvent polarity series: ether < ketone < alcohol < carboxylic acid. Only option (4) fits.
key_check_note: Strictly by gas-phase dipole moment, acetone would be the most polar. The key is consistent only with the standard solvent-polarity (hydrogen-bonding) interpretation, which is clearly what the question intends.
